articles.title: Live airband on all frequencies from KORS. Victoria, CA also ground stopped
articles.summary: Live airband on all frequencies from KORS. Victoria, CA also ground stopped

top_comments: Hi all. Thanks for the interest. I'm going to post an impromptu blog post here just explaining what this is. The rather unfortunate ground stop today made this unexpectedly useful with the pilots here on Orcas just to get a sense of the chatter in our airspace re the situation.This is an ETTUS B210 attached to a dual 4090 box. It's a polyphase channelizer that takes the entire airband, channelizes it using cuda code on GPU, demodulates it, detects transmissions, throws away data tx and then feeds the tx through a voice model I created for transcription. A separate LLM reads the transcriptions to create a situational awareness picture of the airspace.I'm interested in open sourcing this and making it available for folks who can run an ETTUS B210 or high quality SDR with enoguh bandwidth and a local GPU machine, so that we can cover more airpsace.This was born out of an incident we had not too long ago where a pilot around KORS (based at Friday Harbor) lost the engine in his 172, and put it in the water in front of a ferry and was picked up by the ferry. We're a pretty close bunch on Orcas Island and we only heard about it days later via social media. That felt completely unacceptable, and I set out to create a radio that could monitor everything in real-time, all the time, and alert on emergencies. That has extended to transcribing and creating situational awareness for a chunk of airspace.I'm an IFR pilot. I fly a T206H regularly in IMC around here and I'm a ground instructor. You can email me at mark@defiant.com or find me on x at mmaunder if you'd like to connect. I'm particularly interested in hearing from folks who can run a station on their own hardware and are under bravo or a charlie or even just somewhere interesting re airspace.

These are raw transcripts unedited by me that I extracted possibly related to the groundstop, generated at time of posting: 2143Z, 126.400 Victoria Ground (weak signal): "Yeah, we just uh communication issues, so we got the traffic stopped on [unintelligible]" 2151Z, 134.800 Vancouver Centre, pilot of a flight ending "364": "We're saying they just have an alternate plan. They've been getting lower and lower 48 right now. We're on the phone with you, they are saying cannot show any reason why we would be out of communication to Seattle. So just otherwise we do have some alternates that we're talking about, but we just want to see, you see anything on your end that we cannot proceed to Seattle?" 2152Z, 134.800 Vancouver Centre, same pilot: "Okay, sounds good. Yeah, we appreciate that. We'll be staying by and we'll just kind of get the alternate plans for ready to go. Thank you." 2159Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Seacraft 304, just a heads up here, there is a ground stop for an aircraft about into Vancouver at this time. I'm sure you have a VFR slot, seeing where you're headed there now, so I'd like to be still going to take you, but it just has stopped that you might end up getting turned around." 2159Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Sorry, that's all inbound aircraft, ground stop." 2200Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Yeah, it's not affecting anything airborne at this time. We're just about departing anything for Vancouver and Calgary at this time." 2201Z, 126.400 Victoria Ground, pilot (weak signal): "Hey Ground, it's Jazz 270, and I'm guessing there's a flow for Vancouver." 2203Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, pilot: "Uh just wanted to confirm uh there's a ground stop uh going into Vancouver on this frequency?" 2203Z, 121.075 Victoria Terminal, controller: "Encore 3325, that's correct. Nothing is departing to land at Vancouver at this time." 2204Z, 134.800 Vancouver Centre, pilot: "Yeah, right now they said normal ops continue, but we'll see what happens once we get closer." 2217Z, 126.125 Vancouver Departure, pilot: "Yeah, you guys not having any of the issues that they're having in the US right now?" 2217Z, 126.125 Vancouver Departure: "Uh, apparently the ones uh seeing ground stop for the 14 major airports I've just got a few minutes. Okay, thanks." 2227Z, 126.400 Victoria Ground, pilot: "Encore 58, information Papa, requesting flow through to Vancouver for 2255." Reply: "Roger, 2255 on the flight plan."

If you scroll back to 2:03pm (the time this link was posted) there was this interaction:14:03:04 Uh just wanted to confirm uh there's a ground stop uh going into Vancouver on this frequency?14:03:10 Encore 3325, that's correct. Nothing is departing to land at Vancouver at this time.

articles.summary: Ukraine knocks out 36% of Russia's oil refining capacity in under two weeks

top_comments: Refineries are huge, and hitting one doesn't automatically knock it out - Ukraine has actually already hit lots of Russian refineries this year, many of them more than once: https://www.reddit.com/r/RussianHitlists/comments/1ugfpiw/ru...Obviously Russia doesn't publish any data about how long it takes them to repair their refineries, but some of them showed significant damages from the pictures and videos you can find online.

Feels like drones and rockets have created a similar dynamic to mutually assured destruction, except for much smaller actors with far fewer resources. It's not hard to imagine a future where e.g. Taiwan is just armed with so many cheap drones and rockets that for even a great power like China the guarantee of enormous economic damage at home is just not worth it.
IEA says repairs are getting slower: https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/economics-markets/news/...

articles.title: Terminal borders that don't cost a cell
articles.summary: Terminal borders that don't cost a cell

top_comments: A much better alternative to this would be to for more terminal emulators to implement overstrike mode (DECSET 20, as available on the VK100). That way you could just draw border characters over existing text cells to achieve the same thing.Unfortunately mintty is the only terminal emulator I'm aware of which supports overstrike [0], as this would open up a world of new possibilities for TUI apps if more widely supported.[0] https://github.com/mintty/mintty/wiki/CtrlSeqs#overstrike

I love this work and everything else Ratatui does but I have to ask: if you're changing the terminal protocol and the terminal itself to do this, why not do something more ambitious; a full monospaced information-dense UI framework, a terminal designed for user interfaces, rather than one designed to replicate the limitations of dumb terminals?

A pet peeve of mine is that most people / WM get "useless gaps" wrong. You do want a gap between two terminals because otherwise there are times where things can get really confusing (where you don't know what belong to which terminal / window).So the "borderless" (0 pixels) / zero "useless gaps" (which really aren't useless so it's also a complete misnomer) simply are confusing and... Wrong.But then people who do use useless gap, as in TFA, get it wrong too: they typically add gaps near the monitor's edges.Yeah. But no. Sorry but my monitor's edge is a perfectly fine gap. I don't risk mistaking it for anything.So I modified my WM (the Awesome WM) to do proper "useless gaps" computation and remove the ones that really are useless: and that'd be those near the monitor's physical border.I mean: nearly everybody gets it wrong, but it's not complicated to get that right, is it?
